challenge: Think of one task you do regularly. If AI became 10× better tomorrow, which part of that task would become easier—and which part would still require your judgment?
practice: Pick one hour of real work. Label each step as routine execution, judgment, relationship, physical work, or authorization. Then decide where AI should assist, automate, or stay out.

applications.Work: Identify tasks becoming cheaper and the responsibilities becoming more valuable.
applications.Business: Look for repetitive execution that can be delegated while preserving human accountability.
applications.Creator: Use AI to increase output without outsourcing taste, point of view, or audience trust.
applications.Personal Path: Choose one area where AI can multiply your effort without replacing your judgment.

challenge: Imagine two people have access to the same powerful AI. One becomes far more valuable; the other becomes easier to replace. What do you think separates them?
practice: Choose one difficult decision you made recently. Write what was known, what was uncertain, what trade-off mattered, and what evidence would have changed your decision.

applications.Work: Strengthen judgment, communication, trust, and cross-functional coordination.
applications.Business: Make customer trust and accountability part of the operating model, not an afterthought.
applications.Creator: Use AI for possibility generation while keeping taste and originality human-led.
applications.Personal Path: Choose one human capability to deliberately strengthen over the next 30 days.

challenge: Take a task you normally give ChatGPT in one sentence. What information, constraints, tools, and quality checks would a capable employee need to do it reliably?
practice: Rewrite one vague AI request as an Operator Brief: outcome, inputs, allowed sources, constraints, output format, review criteria, and stop conditions.

applications.Work: Turn one recurring task into a repeatable AI-assisted operating procedure.
applications.Business: Design AI around outcomes and controls instead of collecting disconnected tools.
applications.Creator: Build reusable research, drafting, editing, and publishing workflows.
applications.Personal Path: Move from asking AI for answers to designing how AI should help you think and work.

challenge: An AI gives you a confident answer that sounds correct. What would you need to see before you would let that answer affect money, a customer, a job application, or another person?
practice: Take one AI-generated answer and build an evidence chain: claims, sources, assumptions, calculations, risks, and the point where a human should approve or stop the process.

applications.Work: Verify consequential AI output before it reaches customers, decisions, or official records.
applications.Business: Create approval boundaries for money, permissions, contracts, deletion, and other irreversible actions.
applications.Creator: Fact-check claims and distinguish sourced facts from generated interpretation.
applications.Personal Path: Build the habit of asking 'How do I know?' before accepting a fluent answer.

challenge: A process has six steps. Some are fixed rules; others require interpreting messy information. Would you use normal automation, AI, an agent, or a combination? Why?
practice: Map one real workflow from trigger to completion. Mark which steps are deterministic, which require interpretation, which need stored state, and which require human approval.

applications.Work: Automate predictable handoffs while using AI only where interpretation adds value.
applications.Business: Design small, auditable workflows before attempting broad autonomy.
applications.Creator: Connect research, drafting, review, asset storage, and publishing into a controlled workflow.
applications.Personal Path: Learn to choose the simplest system that solves the problem reliably.

challenge: If an AI assistant must answer questions about a company policy that changes every month, should it rely on what the model already 'knows'? What should it rely on instead?
practice: Design a small knowledge base for something you know well. Define the sources, owner, effective date, version, topic, and what should happen when two sources conflict.

applications.Work: Ground assistants in approved policies, SOPs, documentation, and current source material.
applications.Business: Treat knowledge quality, permissions, freshness, and source lineage as part of the product.
applications.Creator: Organize research and source material so AI can retrieve your actual body of work.
applications.Personal Path: Build a trusted knowledge system instead of relying on scattered chats and memory.

challenge: If one AI agent creates an important result and then grades its own work, what could go wrong? How would you design a more trustworthy system?
practice: Design a three-role agent team for one task. Give each role a narrow job, allowed tools, output format, stop condition, and one test case that could expose a failure.

applications.Work: Use specialized agents for bounded tasks and independent review.
applications.Business: Add evaluation and monitoring before giving agents broader authority.
applications.Creator: Separate research, creation, fact-checking, and editorial review when quality matters.
applications.Personal Path: Learn to test an AI system against failure cases instead of judging it from one impressive result.
